evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Early in the time course, immediately after RNA transcription, new TLC1-MS2 molecules localized predominantly in the cytoplasm.
source: In contrast to steady state, early in the time course, i.e. immediately after RNA transcription, new TLC1-MS2 molecules localized predominantly in the cytoplasm (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The predominantly cytoplasmic localization of new TLC1-MS2 molecules persisted for approximately 2 hr.
source: This behavior persisted for approximately 2 hr, followed by gradual return of new molecules to the nucleus and re-establishment of steady state at the end of the time course.
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: New TLC1 molecules gradually return to the nucleus and re-establish steady state at the end of the time course.
source: This behavior persisted for approximately 2 hr, followed by gradual return of new molecules to the nucleus and re-establishment of steady state at the end of the time course.
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: At early stages after transcription, TLC1 molecules are exported to the cytoplasm but eventually shuttle back to the nucleus.
source: We conclude that at early stages after transcription, TLC1 molecules are exported to the cytoplasm but eventually shuttle back to the nucleus.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the smFISH data showing the dynamic localization of new TLC1 molecules.

claim: In xpo1-1 cells kept at the permissive temperature, new TLC1 molecules followed similar localization dynamics as in wild type cells.
source: In xpo1-1 cells kept at the permissive temperature, new TLC1 molecules followed similar localization dynamics as in wild type cells, temporarily localizing in the cytoplasm at early stages and eventually flowing back to the nucleus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In xpo1-1 cells incubated at the restrictive temperature, a drastic accumulation of newly transcribed TLC1 molecules in the nucleus was observed.
source: However, in xpo1-1 cells incubated at the restrictive temperature, a drastic accumulation of newly transcribed TLC1 molecules in the nucleus was observed (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: The accumulation of new TLC1 molecules in the nucleus observed in xpo1-1 cells at 37°C was not due to the increase in temperature.
source: The accumulation of new TLC1 molecules in the nucleus observed in xpo1-1 cells at 37°C was not due to the increase in temperature, as new TLC1 molecules in wild type cells grown at 37°C reached a normal steady state distribution, though with a slightly faster dynamics (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by control experiments with wild type cells at 37°C shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The early temporary export of newly synthesized TLC1 molecules to the cytoplasm depends on the Xpo1 exportin.
source: These data directly demonstrate that the early temporary export of newly synthesized TLC1 molecules to the cytoplasm depends on the Xpo1 exportin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the xpo1-1 mutant data.

claim: Xpo1-mediated transport is the only mechanism responsible for the export of new telomerase RNA.
source: Moreover, Xpo1-mediated transport is the only mechanism responsible for the export of new telomerase RNA, as upon Xpo1 inactivation virtually all TLC1 transcripts are retained in the nucleus for up to 8 hr (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the complete nuclear retention of TLC1 in xpo1-1 mutants.

claim: In xpo1-1 mutants incubated at 37°C, a higher amount of new TLC1-MS2 RNA was detected as compared to wild type cells.
source: Notably, in xpo1-1 mutants incubated at 37°C but not at 25°C, a higher amount of new TLC1-MS2 RNA was detected as compared to wild type cells (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A larger number of new TLC1 foci was observed in xpo1-1 mutant cells at the restrictive temperature.
source: Consistent with the northern blot quantification, we also observed a larger number of new TLC1 foci in xpo1-1 mutant cells at the restrictive temperature (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The increased TLC1 level in xpo1-1 mutants at 37°C is due to inactivation of Xpo1 rather than the elevated temperature.
source: Again, this effect is due to inactivation of Xpo1 rather than the elevated temperature, as wild type cells grown at 30 and 37°C have comparable numbers of new TLC1 foci (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by control experiments with wild type cells at different temperatures shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: In the absence of functional Xpo1 when the cytoplasmic export of TLC1 is completely blocked, newly made telomerase RNA persists in the nucleus and accumulates to higher levels than in export-competent cells.
source: These data show that in the absence of functional Xpo1 when the cytoplasmic export of TLC1 is completely blocked, newly made telomerase RNA persists in the nucleus and accumulates to higher levels than in export-competent cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the xpo1-1 mutant data showing nuclear accumulation and increased TLC1 levels.

claim: For the first 60 min after recombination induction in kap122Δ mutants, newly synthesized TLC1 RNA behaved similarly to wild type cells, localizing predominantly in the cytoplasm.
source: For the first 60 min after recombination induction in kap122Δ mutants, newly synthesized TLC1 RNA behaved similarly to wild type cells, localizing predominantly in the cytoplasm (Figures 2E and 3C).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figures 2E and 3C.

claim: In kap122Δ cells, the nuclear TLC1 fraction began to recuperate only 3 hr after recombination induction and never reached the wild type level.
source: However, in kap122Δ cells, the nuclear fraction began to recuperate only 3 hr after recombination induction and never reached the wild type level, always remaining below 50% of total new molecules (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: By the end of the time course, new TLC1 molecules in kap122Δ mutants had reached the steady state nucleo-cytoplasmic distribution that was characteristic of kap122Δ mutants before recombination induction.
source: In fact, by the end of the time course, new TLC1 molecules had reached the steady state nucleo-cytoplasmic distribution that was characteristic of kap122Δ mutants before recombination induction (Figures 3C, 16 h; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Kap122 supports the rapid re-import of new molecules to the nucleus after the cytoplasmic stage.
source: Therefore, these results show that Kap122 supports the rapid re-import of new molecules to the nucleus after the cytoplasmic stage.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the delayed nuclear re-import in kap122Δ mutants.

claim: The late re-import of new TLC1 into the nucleus in kap122Δ mutants suggests the existence of a secondary RNA import pathway.
source: However, the late re-import of new TLC1 into the nucleus in kap122Δ mutants suggests the existence of a secondary RNA import pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the eventual nuclear re-import in kap122Δ mutants.

claim: Telomere length in kap122Δ mutants with steady state distribution of TLC1 molecules is only slightly shorter than in wild type cells.
source: Indeed, telomere length in kap122Δ mutants with steady state distribution of TLC1 molecules is only slightly shorter than in wild type cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The level of new TLC1-MS2 RNA in kap122Δ mutants is about 2-fold lower than in wild type cells.
source: Consistent with this scenario, the level of new TLC1-MS2 RNA in kap122Δ mutants is about 2-fold lower than in wild type cells, as analyzed by northern blotting (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A similar reduction in the number of new TLC1-MS2 foci in the absence of Kap122 was observed by smFISH.
source: Consistently, a similar reduction in the number of new TLC1-MS2 foci in the absence of Kap122 was also observed by smFISH (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: New cytoplasmic TLC1 molecules, which due to the absence of Kap122 are not rapidly transported back to the nucleus, become prone to degradation.
source: These data indicate that new cytoplasmic TLC1 molecules, which due to the absence of Kap122 are not rapidly transported back to the nucleus, become prone to degradation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced TLC1 levels in kap122Δ mutants.

claim: While a redundant secondary TLC1 import pathway may exist, it is less efficient than the primary Kap122 pathway as it cannot prevent TLC1 losses in the cytoplasm.
source: Therefore, while a redundant secondary TLC1 import pathway may exist, it is less efficient than the primary Kap122 pathway as it cannot prevent TLC1 losses in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the delayed re-import and reduced TLC1 levels in kap122Δ mutants.

claim: Transport of mRNAs, pre-ribosomal subunits and tRNA to the cytoplasm depends on the Mex67 export receptor.
source: Transport of mRNAs, pre-ribosomal subunits and tRNA to the cytoplasm depends on the Mex67 export receptor (Segref et al., 1997; Santos-Rosa et al., 1998; Yao et al., 2007; Faza et al., 2012; Chatterjee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Mex67 is required for the nuclear export of snRNAs.
source: In addition, Mex67 is required for the nuclear export of snRNAs and may be implicated in TLC1 transport (Wu et al., 2014; Becker et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Mex67 may be implicated in TLC1 transport.
source: In addition, Mex67 is required for the nuclear export of snRNAs and may be implicated in TLC1 transport (Wu et al., 2014; Becker et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on literature citations.

claim: At the permissive temperature (25°C), new TLC1-MS2 RNA accumulated efficiently in mex67-5 cells, reaching 80% relative to the recombined reference strain after 8 hr.
source: Northern blot quantification showed efficient accumulation of new TLC1-MS2 RNA at 25°C, which after 8 hr of recombination induction reached 80% relative to the recombined reference strain (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: At the restrictive temperature (37°C), new TLC1 RNA was almost undetectable in mex67-5 cells either by northern blot or smFISH.
source: Surprisingly, at the restrictive temperature, new TLC1 RNA was almost undetectable either by northern blot or smFISH (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is supported by northern blot and smFISH data shown in Figure 4A-D.

claim: The absence of new TLC1 molecules in mex67-5 cells at 37°C was not due to a defect in TLC1-[MS2-IN] recombination.
source: This absence of new TLC1 molecules was not due to a defect in TLC1-[MS2-IN] recombination, as the kinetics of recombination was the same both at 25 and 37°C (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by Southern blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In the absence of Mex67, new TLC1 molecules are either not produced or they are extremely unstable.
source: Therefore, these results suggest that in the absence of Mex67, new TLC1 molecules are either not produced, i.e. the gene is not transcribed, or they are extremely unstable.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of new TLC1 in mex67-5 mutants.

claim: In mex67-5 cells incubated at the restrictive temperature, TLC1 transcription is functional.
source: These data indicate that in mex67-5 cells incubated at the restrictive temperature, TLC1 transcription is functional.
evidence: This is supported by thiolutin experiments and RNA Pol II ChIP data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The level of RNA Pol II detected at the TLC1 locus was comparable in mex67-5 cells grown at 25 and 37°C.
source: In addition, the level of RNA Pol II detected at the TLC1 locus was comparable in mex67-5 cells grown at 25 and 37°C, further confirming that TLC1 transcription is not affected by inactivation of the Mex67 protein (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by RNA Pol II ChIP data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Deletion of RRP6 completely suppressed the mex67-5 phenotype.
source: Strikingly, deletion of RRP6 completely suppressed the mex67-5 phenotype, as in mex67-5 rrp6Δ cells grown at the restrictive temperature, new TLC1 RNA molecules accumulated to the same level as at the permissive conditions (Figure 4C,E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH and northern blot data shown in Figure 4C,E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: In the absence of Mex67, new TLC1 transcripts undergo rapid degradation by the nuclear exosome.
source: These data directly show that in the absence of Mex67, new TLC1 transcripts undergo rapid degradation by the nuclear exosome and indicate that Mex67 is essential for stabilization of TLC1 RNA immediately after transcription and prior to export.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the rescue of TLC1 levels by rrp6Δ deletion.

claim: Mex67 is essential for stabilization of TLC1 RNA immediately after transcription and prior to export.
source: These data directly show that in the absence of Mex67, new TLC1 transcripts undergo rapid degradation by the nuclear exosome and indicate that Mex67 is essential for stabilization of TLC1 RNA immediately after transcription and prior to export.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mex67-5 mutant data and rescue by rrp6Δ deletion.

claim: The stability of pre-existing and matured TLC1 molecules does not seem to be affected by dysfunctional Mex67.
source: At the same time, the stability of pre-existing and matured molecules does not seem to be affected by dysfunctional Mex67 (Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data showing that old TLC1 molecules are stable in mex67-5 mutants.

claim: In mex67-5 xpo1-1 cells grown at the permissive temperature, newly synthesized TLC1 molecules accumulated with normal kinetics.
source: In mex67-5 xpo1-1 cells grown at the permissive temperature, newly synthesized TLC1 molecules accumulated with normal kinetics (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH and northern blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: At 37°C, new TLC1 RNA was almost undetectable in mex67-5 xpo1-1 double mutant, recapitulating the phenotype of mex67-5 cells.
source: However, at 37°C, new TLC1 RNA was almost undetectable in a double mutant, thus completely recapitulating the phenotype of mex67-5 cells.
evidence: This is supported by smFISH and northern blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Mex67 functions upstream of Xpo1, stabilizing newly transcribed TLC1 RNA prior to their cytoplasmic export.
source: These data confirm that Mex67 indeed functions upstream of Xpo1, stabilizing newly transcribed TLC1 RNA prior to their cytoplasmic export.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mex67-5 xpo1-1 double mutant data.

claim: The few TLC1 molecules that remained detectable in mex67-5 cells almost exclusively accumulated at the nuclear periphery.
source: Notably, these remaining TLC1 foci almost exclusively accumulated at the nuclear periphery (Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In mex67-5 rrp6Δ double mutant cells, the vast majority of new molecules displayed nuclear periphery localization.
source: This observation became even more striking in mex67-5 rrp6Δ double mutant cells, in which the vast majority of new molecules displayed this localization (Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Mex67 acts as a prerequisite for the Xpo1-mediated export of TLC1 transcripts.
source: Therefore, in addition to its essential role in stabilizing new TLC1 molecules, Mex67 acts as a prerequisite for the Xpo1-mediated export of TLC1 transcripts.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the nuclear periphery localization of TLC1 in mex67-5 mutants.

claim: Mex67 performs an entirely new and unexpected function in the biogenesis of telomerase RNA.
source: Collectively, the data thus demonstrate that Mex67 performs an entirely new and unexpected function in the biogenesis of telomerase RNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the novel findings about Mex67's role in TLC1 stability.

claim: After export to the cytoplasm, new TLC1 RNA acquires certain features that render it stable in the absence of a functional Mex67 protein.
source: This suggests that after export to the cytoplasm, new TLC1 RNA acquires certain features that render it stable in the absence of a functional Mex67 protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that old TLC1 molecules are stable in mex67-5 mutants.

claim: A mutated tlc1-Sm2T allele disrupts Sm7 binding to TLC1 and renders it unstable.
source: To verify this idea, we took advantage of a mutated tlc1-Sm2T allele which disrupts Sm7 binding to TLC1 and renders it unstable (Seto et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 molecules shuttle to the cytoplasm at the beginning of the time course.
source: At the beginning of the time course, tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 molecules shuttle to the cytoplasm (Figures 5A, B, 1 h).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 molecules never returned to the nucleus and remained in the cytoplasm.
source: However, to our surprise, these molecules never returned to the nucleus and remained in the cytoplasm (Figures 5B, 4 h).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The Sm7 complex is required for re-import of new TLC1 transcripts to the nucleus.
source: This suggests that the Sm7 complex is required for re-import of new TLC1 transcripts to the nucleus.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cytoplasmic retention of tlc1-Sm2T molecules.

claim: The level of tagged tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 RNA remained low over the entire time course.
source: Although the kinetics of TLC1-[Sm2T-MS2-IN] recombination were normal (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), the level of tagged tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 RNA remained low over the entire time course, as detected by northern blotting using the TLC1 or MS2 probes (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: The number of newly synthesized tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 foci was lower than in wild type cells.
source: Consistently, the number of newly synthesized tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 foci was also lower than in wild type cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: New tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 transcripts are unstable.
source: This indicates that new tlc1-Sm2T-MS2 transcripts are unstable, as expected (Seto et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the low levels of tlc1-Sm2T RNA and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Cells with the recombined TLC1-[Sm2T-MS2-IN] locus eventually undergo senescence and switch to a recombination-dependent telomere maintenance with the survivor telomere phenotype.
source: As a result of TLC1 loss, cells with the recombined TLC1-[Sm2T-MS2-IN] locus eventually undergo senescence and switch to a recombination-dependent telomere maintenance with the survivor telomere phenotype (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by telomere length analysis data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Even in the absence of Sm7 binding, newly transcribed TLC1 molecules are processed and exported from the nucleus normally.
source: Since the remaining tlc1-Sm2T RNA accumulates in the cytoplasm (Figure 5B), we hypothesized that even in the absence of Sm7 binding, newly transcribed TLC1 molecules are processed and exported from the nucleus normally, yet they become unstable and disappear after export to the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the cytoplasmic localization of tlc1-Sm2T molecules.

claim: In tlc1-Sm2T xpo1-1 cells grown at the restrictive temperature, new tlc1-Sm2T RNA molecules accumulated in the nucleus and were more abundant than at the permissive conditions.
source: Indeed, in tlc1-Sm2T xpo1-1 cells grown at the restrictive temperature, new tlc1-Sm2T RNA molecules accumulated in the nucleus and were more abundant than at the permissive conditions, when tlc1-Sm2T RNA shuttled to the cytoplasm (Figure 5A,E–G; Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH and northern blot data shown in Figure 5A,E-G.

claim: Newly synthesized telomerase RNA is stable in the nucleoplasm, even without the Sm7 complex.
source: Therefore, our data show that newly synthesized telomerase RNA is stable in the nucleoplasm, even without the Sm7 complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the stabilization of tlc1-Sm2T in xpo1-1 mutants.

claim: The Sm7 complex binds new TLC1 RNA only after its export to the cytoplasm.
source: The Sm7 complex binds new TLC1 RNA only after its export to the cytoplasm, where this association becomes essential for TLC1 stability as well as for re-import of the molecules back into the nucleus.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the tlc1-Sm2T mutant data.

claim: Cytoplasmic association with the Sm7 complex is essential for TLC1 stability.
source: The Sm7 complex binds new TLC1 RNA only after its export to the cytoplasm, where this association becomes essential for TLC1 stability as well as for re-import of the molecules back into the nucleus.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the instability of tlc1-Sm2T molecules in the cytoplasm.

claim: Cytoplasmic association with the Sm7 complex is essential for re-import of TLC1 molecules back into the nucleus.
source: The Sm7 complex binds new TLC1 RNA only after its export to the cytoplasm, where this association becomes essential for TLC1 stability as well as for re-import of the molecules back into the nucleus.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cytoplasmic retention of tlc1-Sm2T molecules.

claim: The cellular pool of telomerase RNA encompasses a variety of molecules at different stages of biogenesis.
source: As for any RNA species, the cellular pool of telomerase RNA encompasses a variety of molecules at different stages of biogenesis.
evidence: This is a general statement about RNA populations.

claim: Conventional imaging methods that rely on RNA-specific probes or tags visualize the total RNA pool and yield information about the steady state RNA distribution.
source: Conventional imaging methods that rely on RNA-specific probes or tags visualize the total RNA pool and therefore yield information about the steady state RNA distribution.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of conventional imaging methods.

claim: The diverse characteristics of various RNA sub-populations generally remain hidden in conventional imaging assays.
source: However, the diverse characteristics of various RNA sub-populations generally remain hidden in such assays.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of conventional imaging methods.

claim: The inducible tagging system allows selective identification and analysis of newly synthesized telomerase RNA transcripts within a heterogeneous TLC1 population.
source: Using a probe specific for the MS2 tag, we can selectively identify and analyze newly synthesized telomerase RNA transcripts within a heterogeneous TLC1 population and track their specific movements by smFISH (Figure 2).
evidence: This describes the capability of the experimental system developed in the study.

claim: The dynamic behavior of TLC1 transcripts that remain untagged after recombination provides clues about the old or matured TLC1 molecules.
source: In addition, the dynamic behavior of TLC1 transcripts that remain untagged after recombination is complete, provides clues about the old or matured TLC1 molecules.
evidence: This describes the utility of the experimental system for studying old TLC1 molecules.

claim: The results provide direct evidence for the nucleo-cytoplasmic TLC1 shuttling model.
source: Thus, our results provide direct evidence for the nucleo-cytoplasmic TLC1 shuttling model and narrow down this process to an early post-transcriptional event.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing temporary cytoplasmic localization of new TLC1.

claim: The nucleo-cytoplasmic shuttling of TLC1 is an early post-transcriptional event.
source: Thus, our results provide direct evidence for the nucleo-cytoplasmic TLC1 shuttling model and narrow down this process to an early post-transcriptional event.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the timing of cytoplasmic localization of new TLC1 molecules.

claim: Telomerase RNA has a very long half-life and can remain functional for much longer than 60 min, exceeding the length of one full cell cycle.
source: Consistent with this idea, telomerase RNA has a very long-half life and can remain functional for much longer than 60 min, exceeding the length of one full cell cycle (Chapon et al., 1997; Larose et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A cooperation of several importins, including Kap122, facilitates a quick and efficient return of new TLC1 transcripts to the nucleus.
source: Therefore, a cooperation of several importins, including Kap122, facilitates a quick and efficient return of new TLC1 transcripts to the nucleus (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data and is illustrated in the model in Figure 6.

claim: Failure or delay in TLC1 re-import may lead to loss of telomerase RNA.
source: Failure or delay in such re-import may lead to loss of telomerase RNA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced TLC1 levels in kap122Δ mutants.

claim: Depletion of Mex67 causes rapid nuclear degradation of all newly transcribed poly-A+ mRNAs.
source: Similar to our results, depletion of Mex67 was shown to cause rapid nuclear degradation of all newly transcribed poly-A+ mRNAs (Tudek et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The vast majority of TLC1 (95%) is generated directly via the Nrd1/Nab3 non-coding RNA termination pathway.
source: It is important to note that the vast majority of TLC1 (95%) is generated directly via the Nrd1/Nab3 non-coding RNA termination pathway (Noël et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: For telomerase RNA, an export block per se does not lead to nuclear RNA decay.
source: This means that at least for telomerase RNA, an export block per se does not lead to nuclear RNA decay.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the stability of TLC1 in xpo1-1 mutants.

claim: Mex67 acts upstream of Xpo1 and plays an unexpected role in stabilization of newly transcribed TLC1 molecules before their cytoplasmic export.
source: This suggests that Mex67 acts upstream of Xpo1 and plays an unexpected role in stabilization of newly transcribed TLC1 molecules before their cytoplasmic export (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data and is illustrated in the model in Figure 6.

claim: Mex67 is known to bind at least to some of its cargoes co-transcriptionally.
source: Mex67 is known to bind at least to some of its cargoes co-transcriptionally (Dieppois et al., 2006; Wende et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Early association of Mex67 with its RNA substrates may assist in proper 3'-end RNA maturation and protection.
source: It has been proposed that such early association with its RNA substrates may assist in proper 3'-end RNA maturation and protection (Forrester et al., 1992; Hammell et al., 2002; Qu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from the literature supported by citations.

claim: Mex67 protects the 3'-end of TLC1 from nuclear degradation by Rrp6.
source: There was some evidence that Mex67 may be able to associate with telomerase RNA (Wu et al., 2014), and our results here firmly establish that Mex67 protects the 3'-end of TLC1 from nuclear degradation by Rrp6 (Figure 4C,E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H; Figure 6).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing rescue of TLC1 by rrp6Δ deletion.

claim: Mex67 may be responsible for a quick delivery of new transcripts to the nuclear pore where they are stabilized and exported by Xpo1.
source: Moreover, since Mex67 can bind to both RNA and nuclear pore components, it may be responsible for a quick delivery of new transcripts to the nuclear pore where they are stabilized and exported by Xpo1.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about Mex67 function.

claim: Mex67 may perform a stabilization function for poly-A+ RNA species as it does for telomerase RNA.
source: Given that Mex67 has been implicated in the life cycle of diverse RNA classes, we speculate that Mex67 may perform a stabilization function for the poly-A+ RNA species as it does for telomerase RNA.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the findings about Mex67 and TLC1.

claim: A cytoplasmic association with the Sm7 complex has been suggested for snRNAs.
source: Recently a cytoplasmic association with the Sm7 complex has also been suggested for snRNAs (Becker et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Nuclear export and cytoplasmic Sm7 binding is a characteristic of mammalian snRNAs.
source: Similarly, nuclear export and cytoplasmic Sm7 binding is also a characteristic of mammalian snRNAs (Fischer et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: In the nucleus, newly synthesized poly-A- telomerase RNA first requires stabilization by Mex67.
source: The new model incorporates the idea that in the nucleus, newly synthesized poly-A- telomerase RNA (Noël et al., 2012) first requires stabilization by Mex67, which may also usher TLC1 to nuclear pores.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Failure to associate with Mex67 results in immediate degradation of new TLC1 transcripts via the nuclear exosome.
source: Failure to associate with Mex67 results in immediate degradation of new TLC1 transcripts via the nuclear exosome.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: TLC1 RNA is transported to the cytoplasm which absolutely requires Xpo1.
source: Next, the RNA is transported to the cytoplasm which absolutely requires Xpo1.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Mex67 may act as an adaptor between TLC1 RNA and Xpo1 exportin.
source: In this regard, our data are consistent with the possibility that Mex67 itself plays this role in addition to its stabilizing function in the nucleus (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: If Mex67 acts as an adaptor between TLC1 RNA and Xpo1 exportin, it would likely translocate through the nuclear membrane with the Xpo1-TLC1 complex.
source: If Mex67 indeed acts as an adaptor between TLC1 RNA and Xpo1 exportin, it would likely translocate through the nuclear membrane with the Xpo1-TLC1 complex.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about Mex67 function.

claim: Once in the cytoplasm, the TLC1 RNA must rapidly associate with the Sm7 complex.
source: Once in the cytoplasm, the TLC1 RNA must rapidly associate with the Sm7 complex, given that Mex67 will likely disembark from the RNA at the nuclear pore exit and get recycled back into the nucleus (Stewart, 2007).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings and literature.

claim: At the cytoplasmic stage, the Sm7 complex is required for TLC1 RNA stabilization.
source: At this stage then, the Sm7 complex is required for TLC1 RNA stabilization, and in turn, TLC1 stability allows for other telomerase subunits to associate with the maturing RNP.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: If Sm7 binding is compromised, TLC1 molecules undergo degradation in the cytoplasm.
source: If this step is compromised, TLC1 molecules undergo degradation in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings with tlc1-Sm2T mutants.

claim: The telomerase RNP is re-imported to the nucleus primarily via Kap122, but alternative and less efficient import pathways do exist.
source: Eventually, the telomerase RNP is re-imported to the nucleus primarily via Kap122, but alternative and less efficient import pathways do exist (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: The final 5'-TMG capping and 3'-end processing of telomerase RNA occurs in the nucleus after its re-import and is dependent on the presence of the Sm7-complex.
source: Finally, our model suggests that the final 5'-TMG capping and 3'-end processing of telomerase RNA occurs in the nucleus after its re-import and is dependent on the presence of the Sm7-complex, possibly analogous to snRNA maturation (Becker et al., 2019).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on inference and analogy to snRNA maturation.

claim: The final maturation step may occur on a relatively mature telomerase RNP.
source: This final step may thus occur on a relatively mature telomerase RNP, which is entirely feasible given a predicted close proximity of the 5'- and 3'-ends of telomerase RNA (Cech, 2004; Dandjinou et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on structural predictions from the literature.

claim: Active telomerase RNPs only contain 5'-TMG capped telomerase RNAs.
source: It is also consistent with the fact that active telomerase RNPs only contain 5'-TMG capped telomerase RNAs (Bosoy et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Maturation of telomerase RNA may serve as a final stabilization step for TLC1 RNA and render it insensitive to loss of Mex67.
source: Maturation of telomerase RNA may also serve as a final stabilization step for TLC1 RNA and render it insensitive to loss of Mex67, as observed above (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observation that old TLC1 is stable in mex67-5 mutants.

claim: The generation and stabilization of human telomerase RNA relies on the association with several proteins, including dyskerin, NHP2 and NOP10 as well as factors involved in the non-coding RNA maturation pathway such as PARN.
source: As in yeast, the generation and stabilization of human telomerase RNA relies on the association with several proteins, including dyskerin, NHP2 and NOP10 as well as factors involved in the non-coding RNA maturation pathway such as PARN (Hoareau-Aveilla et al., 2006; Fu and Collins, 2007; Walne et al., 2007; Moon et al., 2015; Nguyen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Mutations in PARN, dyskerin or NOP10 cause severe genetic disorders.
source: Mutations in PARN, dyskerin or NOP10 cause severe genetic disorders, emphasizing the functional significance of these telomerase subunits and RNA maturation mechanisms (Vulliamy et al., 2006; Walne et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The loss of telomerase RNA due to PARN mutations is amenable to reversion by small molecules.
source: Furthermore, the loss of telomerase RNA due to PARN mutations is amenable to reversion by small molecules that thus may alleviate the severe associated disease (Brenner and Nandakumar, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Inducible RNA tagging tools should greatly aid in teasing out maturation steps and may provide missing links in human telomerase biogenesis.
source: Inducible RNA tagging tools as described in this study should greatly aid in teasing out these maturation steps and may provide missing links in human telomerase biogenesis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the methodology.
